name: refined-denizenscript
description: Denizen scripting for VS Code — highlighting, completion, hover and diagnostics, with an optional .NET-free language server.
author: Humusus_ and DenizenTeam

denizenscript.autoInsertTagSeparators.description: Pressing space directly inside a <map[...]> types ';' and inside a <list[...]> types '|'. Never fires inside a quoted value, outside those two tags, or where there is nothing to separate. One Backspace turns the separator back into a plain space.

denizenscript.inlineArgumentHints.markdownDescription:
Show the arguments a command still accepts as grey text at the end of the line you are editing. Only the line the caret is on is annotated.

To keep them but see them **on demand only**, leave this on and set `#editor.inlayHints.enabled#` to `offUnlessPressed` — the hint then appears while you hold `Ctrl+Alt`.

Needs the TypeScript language server engine: the C# engine has no signature-help implementation, so nothing is shown there.

denizenscript.evaluateMathTags.markdownDescription:
Hovering an arithmetic tag such as `<element[1].sub[<element[2].mul[3]>]>` shows what it works out to. Anything the server would have to answer — definitions, flags, `<player...>` — is listed as a value to supply instead of being guessed at; the **Evaluate Math Tag** command asks for those and shows the result.

A result that is not exactly representable is labelled as rounded: Denizen's internal number representation cannot be determined from its documentation, so the exact digits are not promised.

enumDescriptions: The original .NET server. Stable, and catches the most problems overall.

No .NET dependency, faster start. Completion, hover and most diagnostics work, but tag/command validation isn't wired up yet -- a bad tag or undefined <[definition]> can go unreported -- and there is no event completion, tag hover, deprecation warnings, or cross-file analysis.

denizenscript.server.extra_sources.markdownDescription:
Extra meta documentation sources (direct .zip archive URLs) to load alongside the official Denizen sources.

They are loaded **after** the official ones, so a command or tag defined in both is taken from yours — that is how a fork overrides the upstream definition. Anything your fork *removes* is a different matter: loading is additive, so the upstream entry survives. Use `#denizenscript.server.replace_default_sources#` for that.

Only used by the TypeScript language server engine (`denizenscript.server.engine: "typescript"`); the C# engine uses `denizenscript.extra_sources` instead.

denizenscript.server.replace_default_sou.description: Use denizenscript.server.extra_sources INSTEAD of the official Denizen sources rather than alongside them. For a Denizen fork: loading a fork additively can only ever ADD to the official meta, so anything the fork REMOVED is still offered by completion and still accepted by the checker. Ignored when extra_sources is empty. Only affects the TypeScript engine, and is read once when the server starts, so changing it requires a window reload.

denizenscript.server.tagTracing.description: Narrow tag completions to the tags valid for the traced return type of the preceding tag part, instead of offering every tag part that exists. Turn this off to always see the full list — useful when a tag's real runtime type differs from its documented one, such as a flag or definition holding an object of another type. Only affects the TypeScript engine, and is read once when the server starts, so changing it requires a window reload to take effect.

refinedDenizenscript.mapTag.showExpandLe.description: Show a clickable 'Expand tag' lens above lines containing a multi-entry <map[...]> or <list[...]> tag. The expanded view is editable and writes back as a single line; the file never holds the multi-line form, which Denizen's parser would reject.
